note: Facts and sources behind the member descriptions in RI.json, gathered 2026-10-05. "review" holds research notes for a human check; "issues" lists open questions.

byways.name: Shannock Road
byways.where: Charlestown and Richmond, 1.7 miles from Route 2 to Route 112

facts.fact: 1.7 miles from Route 2 to Route 112 in Charlestown and Richmond, designated January 1991; passes marshes, woodland and stone-walled farm fields.
Midway lies Shannock Village, a small nineteenth-century textile mill village listed in the National Register of Historic Places.
Shannock is a mill village on the Pawcatuck River, which forms the Richmond-Charlestown line; the village runs along Old Shannock Road and Shannock Village Road between two river crossings.

byways.review: RIDOT GIS names the segments Old Shannock Rd and Shannock Village Rd (SCENIC = 1).

byways.name: Ministerial Road
byways.where: Route 110, South Kingstown, 6 miles from Route 1 to Route 138

facts.fact: Ministerial Road is Route 110, six miles from Route 1 to Route 138 in South Kingstown, designated September 1991.
It passes upland forest known for mountain laurel and rhododendron, glacial kettle holes and Larkin Pond, with stone walls from former farmland.
Overhanging trees meet to form a leaf tunnel over the narrow-shouldered road, which skirts the Great Swamp.

byways.name: Veterans Memorial Parkway
byways.where: East Providence, 2.4 miles from Second Street to Route 103

facts.fact: 2.4 miles from Second Street to Route 103 in East Providence along the Providence River, with views of the downtown Providence skyline; designated November 1991.
Built between 1910 and 1920 to a design by the Olmsted firm as part of the Greater Metropolitan Park Plan for Providence.
Lined with mature maple, oak, black pine and sycamore; passes Squantum Woods, Watchemoket Cove and the Fort Hill Overlook.

byways.name: Paradise Avenue and Associated Roads
byways.where: Middletown, 8.3-mile network: Paradise Ave, Berkeley Ave, Wyatt Rd, Mitchell's Lane, Wapping Rd, Peckham Ave, Indian Ave, Hanging Rock Rd

facts.fact: An 8.3-mile network of Middletown roads designated May 1993, lined with historic houses from colonial to Victorian.
The roads pass Paradise Rock and Hanging Rock, blue-gray stone quarried by the Peckham family since 1844, and lead to the Sakonnet River, Sachuest Beach, Sachuest Point and the Norman Bird Sanctuary.
Where Paradise Avenue reaches Second Beach, views open south to Narragansett Bay and the Purgatory Chasm bluffs; the historic property Whitehall sits on Berkeley Avenue.

byways.review: The state lists 8.3 miles; the catalog line maps 7.3.

byways.name: Great Road/Breakneck Hill Road
byways.where: Route 123, Lincoln, 1.4 miles from Route 146 to Manchester Print Works Road

facts.fact: 1.4 miles of Route 123 in Lincoln across the Moshassuck River valley, designated June 1993, past open fields, Chase Farm and a towering sycamore.
Great Road dates to 1683 as one of Rhode Island's earliest colonial roads; the Great Road Historic District includes the 1687 Eleazer Arnold House, a stone-ender, and Hearthside, built in 1810.
Chase Farm was a large dairy operation in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries; views from Great Road take in Butterfly Pond, the Moshassuck River, Hearthside and the Arnold House.

byways.name: Route 102
byways.where: Exeter, 7.3 miles between Route 2 and Route 3 (Ten Rod Road)

facts.fact: 7.3 miles of Route 102 in Exeter between Route 2 and Route 3, designated September 1993; most of it follows the eighteenth-century Ten Rod Road, still bounded by stone walls.
The road crosses north-south hills up to 560 feet high and five valleys holding headwater streams of the Queen's River.
It once carried goods and livestock to market at the colonial port of Wickford; red maples in the valleys turn scarlet in autumn.

byways.review: RIDOT GIS shows the segments as Ten Rod Rd and Victory Hwy (SCENIC = 6).

byways.name: Route 114
byways.where: Bristol, 5 miles of Route 114 (Hope Street, Ferry Road) and High Street, Warren town line to Mount Hope Bridge

facts.fact: Five miles of Route 114 (Hope Street and Ferry Road) and High Street in Bristol from the Warren line to the Mount Hope Bridge, designated August 2000, under a nearly continuous canopy of mature trees.
Passes through a seventeenth-century planned grid town past Colt State Park and Blithewold, with side streets ending in views of Bristol Harbor.
The Bristol Fourth of July Parade, founded in 1785, is part of the oldest Independence Day celebration in the United States.

byways.name: Route 1 (Charlestown)
byways.where: US 1 (Post Road), Charlestown, 7 miles from the South Kingstown line to the Westerly line

facts.fact: Seven miles of Route 1, the Post Road, across Charlestown from the South Kingstown line to the Westerly line, designated August 2002.
Wooded Charlestown Moraine lines the north side and a wide planted median divides much of the road, while lower vegetation on the south side gives glimpses of the salt ponds.
Historic sites along it include the 1667 Stanton Inn and the Wilcox Tavern; Burlingame, the state's largest campground, is on the road.

byways.review: Not in the catalog; draw from RIDOT layer with SCENIC = 8.

byways.name: Route 1 (South Kingstown)
byways.where: US 1 (Post Road, Tower Hill Road), South Kingstown, 12.35 miles, Charlestown line to North Kingstown line excluding a half mile in Narragansett

facts.fact: 12.35 miles of Route 1 within South Kingstown, designated May 2018; a half-mile piece in Narragansett is excluded.
Views take in Point Judith Pond, Silver Spring Cove and Mill Pond, and on clear days Aquidneck Island and Newport across Narragansett Bay; about four miles of stone walls parallel the road.
The Observation Tower and Hannah Robinson Rock stand at the Route 138 intersection, and the road crosses Ministerial Road.

byways.review: Not in the catalog; draw from RIDOT layer with SCENIC = 9. Official page is the Town of South Kingstown's stewardship plan page (RIDOT links it).

issues: Route 1 (Charlestown) and Route 1 (South Kingstown) are not in the catalog; give them lines from the RIDOT layer (SCENIC = 8 and SCENIC = 9). Both include both carriageways of divided US 1 and some ramp segments (NAME 'EXIT', 'US HWY 1 N/S'); a draw may want to drop NAME LIKE 'EXIT%' or keep one carriageway.

GIS code SCENIC = 71 mixes the Middletown Paradise Avenue network with Bristol's High Street and a Washington St piece (the High Street part of the Route 114 designation). Route 114 proper is SCENIC = 7.

The registry note mentions a national Revolutionary Heritage Byway; I found no nationally designated byway in Rhode Island on the RIDOT page and the catalog has none for RI, so nothing is listed as a second program. Worth a check that the note is not a mix-up with another state.
The GIS layer lives on gisstage.dot.ri.gov (staging host name). It works and is what the RIDOT story map uses, but it could move.
Route 1 (South Kingstown) has no RIDOT stewardship PDF; RIDOT links the town's page, which presents a working draft plan.
Route 102, Route 114 and Route 1 Charlestown stewardship PDFs are scanned images (no text layer); facts for those come from the RIDOT program page.
